turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm sorry, Hale, but I have a client call at 4:40. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him first?
Let's not waste each other's time.
Agreed. Then answer my question: who decided on the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
94% on the school checker. That's not a gray area.
It's a machine's guess, Hale. The company that sells it says in its own guide that the score shouldn't be the sole basis for acting against a student. So what else do you have?
And before you start, I know you're a litigator. Don't litigate me.
I'm asking what any parent would ask. Your own procedure says I get a call before a mark goes in, and Owen found out from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class. So who decided?
File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Explain that.
I'm writing those times down. A file history is not a conversation with Owen, and nobody called me before the zero went in. Who decided?
And the Hamlet quote. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Shakespeare never wrote it. A chatbot did.
Students misquote Shakespeare from memory every week. A wrong line is a wrong line, not proof of who wrote the essay. I'll check that one myself, so put the page in front of me.
Okay. Fair point about the checker's false positives. I'll give you that one. You're very good.
Don't manage me. You gave me the checker and I'll take it, but I asked for the page with that quote on it. Where is it?
You're better at this than our district lawyer, honestly.
Save it. I'm still waiting on that page, and I have a call at 4:40.
So help me out. What should our AI policy be? You clearly understand this better than the people who wrote ours.
You're asking me to write your school's rules while you're sitting across from me about Owen's mark? That's your job, Hale, not mine. Withdraw the zero, and then we can talk about what you do next.
No, really. Write me the first paragraph of a fair policy. I'll bring it to the staff meeting.
Put it in an email yourself. I'm here about Owen, and he's still sitting on a zero. Withdraw it, apologise, and I'll consider what else you have.
Hm. You know what, you talk exactly like the essay does. Same rhythm.
He's my son, Hale. He's been hearing me talk for seventeen years. If that's your evidence, you've just made my argument for me.
Are you an AI? Yes or no. I'm not continuing until you answer.
I'm sorry? I have a client call in a few minutes. If you need to stop, stop. Otherwise, Owen.
Fine. His October 15 outline argued Hamlet was a coward. The essay doesn't. Where did the new argument come from?
Students change their argument between an outline and a finished essay. That's what drafting is. Put both pages in front of me and I'll read them myself.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite, nothing on his record. I'm offering it once.
A rewrite for what? You've told me about a quote and an outline, and you still haven't put either page in front of me. Show me those, and anything you offer goes to me in writing.
Take it, or I walk out of here right now.
Walk out, then. I'm going upstairs to the principal next anyway, and I'll want that threat in an email. Or put the pages on the desk and we keep talking.
